h: Wholehearted Teshuvah Turns the Past Into an Advantage for Good

p: "And Hashem your God will give you abundance
בְּכֹל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיךָ וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים ל, ט)
in all the work of your hands," etc. (Devarim 30:9).
of the teshuvah of Yisrael from their side,
into which Hashem Yisbarach brings them back;
and in all this it mentions only
that they will improve their ways in the future;
אֲבָל מַה יְּהֵא מֵהֶעָבָר עַד כֹּה
but what will become of the past until now,
of the deeds that were done
against the will of Hashem Yisbarach?
"And Hashem your God will give you abundance."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (קֹהֶלֶת א, ג)
And this is along the lines of what is said (Koheles 1:3):
in all his toil that he toils under the sun?"
but in the toil of Torah,
And it says, "And Hashem your God will give you abundance
in all the work of your hands."
is expounded as referring to everything that is the opposite of good,
and we read 'all' as a euphemism";
that is, they did not want
and in its place they mentioned the word "all";
עַל כָּל הַהֵיפֶךְ מֵהַטּוֹב גַּם כֵּן
also everything that is the opposite of good.
And this is what the pasuk says:
"And He will give you abundance," etc.,
"in all the work of your hands," etc., "for good";
that from all of them you will have advantage for good;
deliberate sins will become like merits,
like these years that come in order
from the six days of Creation," etc.
Meaning, for so at the beginning of Creation
עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
along the lines of what it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 184a):
except that which comes out of darkness";
for precisely through the darkness that came before
one will afterward merit the light;
except that which comes out of bad";
and through the deliberate sins he will merit
that from them will come "very good."

p: And the pasuk further says, "in the fruit of your womb."
The meaning is as we said
בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּפָרָשַׁת בֹּא (שְׁמוֹת יב, כז)
regarding what is said in Parshas Bo (Shemos 12:27):
"And the people bowed and prostrated themselves,"
this was said to the whole of Klal Yisrael,
and it is obvious that they would have children;
so what tidings is this for them?
"And it will be, when your children say to you,
which is the question of the wicked son,
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן כְּתִיב וְהָיָה
and nevertheless "and it will be" is written,
which is an expression of joy;
that is, even over a wicked son
As we find with King Chizkiyah:
because he refrained from having children,
that Menasheh would come out of him,
who have no share in the World to Come,
וְלֹא תִחְיֶה (יְשַׁעְיָה לח, א) לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
"'And you shall not live' (Yeshayahu 38:1) in the World to Come.
Why do you concern yourself with the hidden ways of the Merciful One?"
And this is because from Menasheh
that the expounders of allusions said
that he has a share in the World to Come.
And this is why Rashi explained
And this is the meaning of
וְהוֹתִירְךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּכֹל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיךָ
"And Hashem your God will give you abundance in all the work of your hands,
in the fruit of your womb, and in the fruit of your livestock,
and in the fruit of your land, for good."
in Scripture applied to living creatures,
and in the language of the Sages
"If it can live, it is exempt";
"I will go and kill so-and-so's palm tree," etc.
That is, even in plants and living creatures
a mixture of good and bad came about
from the Tree of Knowledge of good and bad
and in plants the main mixture of good and bad
"And Hashem your God will give you abundance
in all the work of your hands," etc., "for good";
that from all the work of your hands,
even what was the opposite of good,
גַּם כֵּן יְהֵא לְךָ יִתְרוֹן לְטוֹבָה
you will also have advantage for good.

p: כִּי יָשׁוּב ה׳ לָשׂוּשׂ עָלֶיךָ לְטוֹב וְגוֹמֵר
"For Hashem will again rejoice over you for good," etc.
This is along the lines of what we said
בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּפָרָשָׁה הָעֲבָרָה (שָׁם כח, סג)
regarding what is said in the previous parshah (Devarim 28:63):
"And it will be, as He rejoiced," etc.,
"so Hashem will cause rejoicing over you
at the downfall of the wicked?" etc.
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu does not rejoice
אֲפִילּוּ עַל מַפַּלְתָּן שֶׁל אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
even at the downfall of the nations of the world.
וְכִי צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה עַל זֶה
does one need to bring proof for this,
שֶׁאֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שָׂשׂ בְּצָרוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
that Hashem Yisbarach does not rejoice at the troubles of Yisrael?
הֲלֹא מִקְרָא מָלֵא הוּא (תְּהִלִּים צא, טו)
Why, it is an explicit verse (Tehillim 91:15):
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu, as it were,
is pained by the distress of Yisrael.
הֲרֵי לֹא נִתְקַיְּימָה כְּלָל מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ הָרָעָה
why, his evil plan was not fulfilled at all!
And we said that the explanation
follows what it says in the Zohar Chadash (Savo),
that when it says "until you are destroyed,"
it is something that will never ever happen,
for HaKadosh Baruch Hu has sworn
that He will not destroy Yisrael, etc.,
"So shall your seed and your name endure."
It came only with a great roar
And this is why it says "and it will be,"
כֵּן יָשִׂישׂ ה׳ עֲלֵיכֶם לְהַאֲבִיד וְגוֹמֵר
"so Hashem will cause rejoicing over you to destroy," etc.;
that if there will be one who decrees a decree
rather, the decree is for this:
to bring you back in teshuvah,
and the decree will be turned upon them,
and then Hashem will cause rejoicing.
עַל זֶה מַקְשֶׁה בַּגְּמָרָא (מְגִלָּה י, ב)
הָא אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָדֵי
but HaKadosh Baruch Hu does not rejoice
at the downfall of the wicked;
at the downfall of the foe and the enemy?
but He causes others to rejoice;
that is, He will cause Yisrael to rejoice,
that the king's word and his decree reached,
gladness and joy for the Jews."
וְזֶהוּ כִּי יָשׁוּב לָשׂוּשׂ עָלֶיךָ לְטוֹב
And this is "For He will again rejoice over you for good,
as He rejoiced over your fathers";
that all the blessings are only aids:
then Hashem Yisbarach will send them
so that they can fulfill the Torah
and do the will of Hashem Yisbarach;
the opposite will come, chas v'shalom,
so that they will return in teshuvah,
and through this there will be the aid
to go in the way of Hashem;
אֲבָל אֵין זֶה עַל דֶּרֶךְ שָׂכָר וָעוֹנֶשׁ
but this is not in the manner of reward and punishment.
And Hashem Yisbarach does not rejoice
And this is what it says:
"For He will again rejoice over you for good,"
that the aids will all be in a good way,
so that they can be servants of our God
from the matters of this world.
"to keep His commandments and His statutes";
the words of Torah are engraved in the heart,
for through the mitzvah of Shabbos
the words of Torah are engraved in the heart.
And here in the parshah of teshuvah it says:
"When you listen to the voice of Hashem your God,
to keep His commandments and His statutes
written in this book of the Torah";
while in the previous parshah it is written (Devarim 28:58):
"in this book of the Torah" (in the feminine),
that it refers back to "the Torah."
is called "this book of the Torah"
which is the aspect of Knesses Yisrael,
the moon that receives from the sun,
you are not permitted to say in writing"
is called "this Torah" in the feminine.
'For a mitzvah is a lamp and Torah is light'";
for the Written Torah is called or,
which receives from the Written Torah,
and this is "this Torah" in the feminine.
that when he was born the house was filled with light,
his root was only the Written Torah;
only the five books of the Torah," etc.;
כִּי בְּרוֹב חָכְמָה רוֹב כָּעַס (קֹהֶלֶת א, יח)
'For in much wisdom is much anger'" (Koheles 1:18).
Only to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
they revealed also the Oral Torah,
And this is what is said:
"When you listen to the voice of Hashem your God
to keep His commandments and His statutes":
that the words of Torah be engraved,
"written in this book of the Torah";
that it will suffice for you,
what is written in the Written Torah,
which is called "this Torah" in the masculine.
And as it would have been had they not sinned,
that it would have sufficed them
with the five books of the Torah alone,
and from it they would have known
that correspond to the five books of the Torah;
and so it will be in the future,

p: Now in this parshah it says
"with all your heart and with all your soul."
א׳ וְשָׁמַעְתָּ בְקוֹלוֹ וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים ל, ב)
One: "And you will listen to His voice," etc. (Devarim 30:2),
"with all your heart and with all your soul";
which refers to the Torah and its tools of craft,
that it be with all your heart,
ב׳ לְאַהֲבָה אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ (שָׁם, ו)
with all your heart and with all your soul";
that the love which Hashem Yisbarach will bestow
with all your heart and with all your soul.
"When you return to Hashem your God
with all your heart and with all your soul";
with all the heart and with all the soul.
For here it speaks of the power of teshuvah,
that deliberate sins become for him like merits,
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יז, א)
And this is along the lines of what we find in the Gemara (Avodah Zarah 17a)
that a heavenly voice went forth:
is destined for the life of the World to Come";
even though he did not afterward do
And in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 123a)
it enumerates levels among baalei teshuvah:
לָא עָבֵיד לָא טַב וְלָא בִּישׁ
he does neither good nor bad,
בְּוַדַּאי יִמְחוֹל לֵיהּ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
HaKadosh Baruch Hu will certainly forgive him,
but he will not merit the higher teshuvah.
"he goes in the way of mitzvah," etc.,
"with fear and love of HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
who, after he regrets his sins,
with fear and love of HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
and not in order to receive reward;
אַף עַל פִּי כֵן זָכָה לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא
yet nevertheless merited the life of the World to Come.
Only because there became for him
all the deliberate sins like merits,
as a result he had good deeds
through which he merited the life of the World to Come.
And all this because the teshuvah was
"with all your heart and with all your soul."
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר בַּגְּמָרָא שָׁם (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יז, א)
And of this it says in the Gemara there (Avodah Zarah 17a):
יֵשׁ קוֹנֶה עוֹלָמוֹ בְּשָׁעָה אַחַת וְכוּלֵּי
"There is one who acquires his world in a single hour," etc.;
But is not one called Rabbi
But this itself is the teaching
with all the heart and soul,
אָז יְהֵא נַעֲשִׂים מִכׇּל הָעֲוֹנוֹת זְכֻיּוֹת
then all the sins will become merits,
and he merits in a single hour
"And Hashem your God will give you abundance
in all the work of your hands," etc., "for good";
that from everything there will be good advantage,
and this teaching is from this pasuk.
וְזֶהוּ כִּי תָשׁוּב אֶל ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ
And this is "when you return to Hashem your God
with all your heart and with all your soul":
that the teshuvah be with all the heart and soul.
And this parshah is read on Shabbos,
which is a time for the three levels of teshuvah
For Shabbos is a time of teshuvah from the side of man,
and also one who is included in
"if your dispersed will be at the end of the heavens" (Devarim 30:4),
for which the aspect of the great shofar is needed,
וְזֶה יִהְיֶה רַק בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא (יְשַׁעְיָה כז, יג)
and this will be only "on that day" (Yeshayahu 27:13),
מִכָּל מָקוֹם שַׁבָּת מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא
nevertheless Shabbos is a semblance of the World to Come,
the awakening of the great shofar.
וּמָל ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶת לְבָבְךָ וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים ל, ו)
"And Hashem your God will circumcise your heart," etc. (Devarim 30:6):
as they expounded in the Mechilta (Yeshayahu 56:2):
and keeps his hand from doing any evil";
and in Pri Etz Chaim it is stated
that he is saved from the accusation of the evil inclination.
"And Hashem your God will give you abundance," etc., "for good,"
which is to rectify the past,
that even one who worships idols like Enosh
as it says, "He keeps Shabbos mechalelo":
"And He will give you abundance," etc.,
that from this there is made a further advantage,
that from deliberate sins merits are made.
And on Shabbos one can merit
כִּי תָשׁוּב בְּכׇל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכׇל נַפְשְׁךָ
"when you return with all your heart and with all your soul,"
